display.purpose: The couple's names in the photograph's sky; min(min(17, 110/L)vw, min(80, 520/L)px) for a longest name of L letters (7 letters: min(15.7vw, 74px)).

script-title.purpose: Every section title, in script gold.

script-closing.purpose: The names that sign the page.

script-name.purpose: The names on the invitation card: max(34px, 11.5cqi) (42px fallback), 1.02, hero ink #4f2f12.

script-joiner.purpose: The invitation card's 'va' between two mirrored leaf sprigs (8.5cqi, line gold): max(20px, 6.6cqi) (24px fallback), script gold.

script-print.purpose: The couple's names printed across both doors of the closed card at 35% height, bronze #8a6128; min(0.13, 2.1/L) of the card width for L characters (L at least 8).

arabic.purpose: The Bismillah at the head of the invitation card (max(13px, 4cqi), 1.4, script gold), only when the couple asks for it; Amiri, loaded as a text= subset of those glyphs only.

numeral.purpose: Countdown tiles, tabular lining figures, shrinking with the tile.

gift-number.purpose: The card number on the To‘yana gift card: four groups of four spread across the card, tabular lining, sepia ink.

scratch-value.purpose: Revealed day, month and year on the scratch cards, in bronze.

lead.purpose: Hero greeting (italic), timeline titles, gallery lead.

small.purpose: Form labels, closing long date (0.18em), showcase text link.

label.purpose: KUN / OY / YIL under the scratch cards, uppercase.

tap-label.purpose: 'Lentani torting' at 80% height on the closed card: 3.1% of the card width, weight 500, 0.32em, uppercase, #6a5236 on the hint glow.

card-caps.purpose: Invitation card: the families and the invitation line in balanced uppercase lines, max(9px, 2.4cqi), 1.75, 0.16em, ink-soft; weekday and time the same size at 0.22em; month and year max(9.5px, 2.7cqi) at 0.2em in ink.

card-verse.purpose: Rum 30:21 in Uzbek on the invitation card, italic, four lines, ink-soft; its reference upright caps at max(8.5px, 2.2cqi), 0.18em, #9a7a48. The address uses the same italic at max(9.5px, 2.6cqi), 1.5.

card-venue.purpose: The venue name on the invitation card, sentence case, ink.

card-day.purpose: The day numeral in the invitation card's date row, lining, hero ink, between gold hairlines rgba(184, 146, 74, 0.75).

shadows.name: gold-surface-hover
shadows.purpose: Gold button hover.

shadows.purpose: Music coin.

shadows.name: scratch-card
shadows.purpose: Scratch date cards.

shadows.name: scratch-focus
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on a scratch card.

shadows.name: card-on-paper
shadows.purpose: The invitation card lying on the page (.mh-card--section).

shadows.name: gift-card
shadows.purpose: Gilt edge, pale inner frame and warm drop of the To‘yana card; the number reads as stamped.

shadows.name: wax-drop
shadows.purpose: The closing seal.

shadows.name: flap-cast
shadows.value: rgba(90, 62, 26, 0.2) clipped to the flap, filter: blur(4px), offset 3-4px toward the point
shadows.purpose: Each inner flap on the paper beneath it; fades over 350ms at 3250ms.

shadows.name: seam

shadows.name: fold-lines

shadows.name: sky-halo

shadows.name: hint-glow

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: Input focus halo with a gilt border.

shadows.name: phone-frame
shadows.purpose: Showcase phone bezel.

shadows.name: stamp-ring
shadows.value: 1.5px solid rgba(184, 146, 74, 0.6) at 4% inset; scale 0.7 to 2.8, fading
shadows.purpose: The ring that leaves the closing seal as it is stamped (900ms after 480ms).

shadows.name: petal-shade
shadows.purpose: Falling petals over the photograph section only.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default: text unblur, photo settle, scratch foil fade, after-date collapse, button press, music coin, showcase card lift.

motion.name: tied-hold
motion.purpose: Closed card tilts in perspective(1600px) around its centre: rotateX 0.7deg / rotateY -0.9deg to rotateX -0.6deg / rotateY 0.9deg, scale 1.03.

motion.name: bow-idle
motion.purpose: The bow (inner layer) swells to 1.025 and rocks 0.6deg and back; the hint breathes 0.55 to 1 opacity on the same beat.

motion.name: pull-tension
motion.value: rubber(d, max) = sign(d) * max * (1 - 1 / (|d| / (1.8 * max) + 1)); max 34px across, 26px down
motion.purpose: While dragging, the bow follows the finger (--px, --py, --pr 0.22deg/px), each band half pivots on its outer end and lengthens to meet the knot (--bl/--br, --bls/--brs), the tails turn -0.5deg/px and stretch 1 + distance/160 (--tail, --tails).

motion.name: pull-release
motion.purpose: Let go early, the satin springs back to the knot with a slight overshoot; a pull that opens sets data-pull to the side the finger went (left when dx < -4).

motion.name: fingertip-press
motion.purpose: Every touch on the closed card presses a soft dent into the paper where it lands.

motion.name: open-press
motion.purpose: Haptic navigator.vibrate([8, 920, 14]) (a touch, then the knot giving); ribbon sounds and music start; hold, bow swell and hint stop; hint fades (0.4s); the card stops taking input.

motion.name: open-camera
motion.purpose: mh-camera (drawn envelope): card gives under the thumb (1.03 to 1.018 by 3%), held nearly still while it opens (1 by 70%), then moves slowly through it to 1.12 (cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.2, 1)).

motion.name: open-untie
motion.purpose: Bow presses to 0.975 by 6% and recovers by 12%; rocks toward the pulled side (4deg x dir at 1.01 by 35%, -2.5deg by 41%, 1deg by 46%); falls like light fabric to --fall (38% of the card height) rocking 6deg / -2deg with 3-4px drift, lands at 80%, folds to 1.04 x 0.7 by 86%, fades from 93% to 1 x 0.72.

motion.name: open-tails
motion.purpose: Pulled tail drawn out under rising tension to ±16deg and 1.32 by 74% (cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.75, 0.5)), slack the instant the knot gives (∓5deg, 1.08 by 88%), settles at ±2deg, 1.1. Free tail swings 9deg, -4deg, 3deg, stretching to 1.12.

motion.name: open-loops
motion.value: pulled loop 260ms, 700ms cubic-bezier(0.6, 0, 0.85, 0.3); other loop 880ms, 320ms cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.9, 0.5)
motion.purpose: Each loop slips through the knot, narrowing toward the centre: rotate ∓38deg, scale 0.12 x 0.45, fade. The pulled side (data-pull, --dir) goes first and slowly.

motion.name: open-knot
motion.purpose: Knot pinches to 0.35 x 0.6 and fades.

motion.name: open-band
motion.purpose: Band halves (inner layers) hold to 35%, go slack (±3deg, 2px, skewX ∓4deg by 41%; 6px by 46%), ripple down with alternating skew (±5deg, ∓3deg) and 2-3px drift through 60% and 70%, land at ±7deg by 80%, fold to 0.92 x 0.5 by 86%, fade from 93% at 0.9 x 0.5.

motion.name: open-doors
motion.purpose: Lift, flex, settle in perspective(1600px): edge lifted to ∓9deg with 0.6deg skewY by 15% (cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.4, 1)), a breath to ∓11deg by 23%, swing past to ∓177deg by 86% (cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.12, 1)), settle at ∓172deg. Fronts darken from 2350/2750ms (1200ms ease-in); shadows cross the paper (1400ms ease-in-out).

motion.name: open-inner-flaps
motion.purpose: Each flap lifts 12deg by 18% (ease-out), then folds back to 165deg (cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.15, 1)) in perspective(1600px); flap shadows fade 400ms ease-out from 3650ms.

motion.name: photo-settle
motion.purpose: Hero photograph (.mh-hero[data-play]) scales 1.12 to 1.04, resting enlarged so the drift never shows an edge. --t0 is 3700ms into the drawn envelope, 0ms at a film's hand-over.

motion.name: photo-focus
motion.purpose: The photograph comes into focus as the paper or the film leaves it: blur(7px) brightness(1.1) to sharp.

motion.name: write
motion.purpose: Handwriting wipe (mh-write): mask linear-gradient(90deg, #000 40%, transparent 60%), mask-size 250% 100%, position 100% to 0. Hero names at --t0 + 250ms + i x 120ms (i 3, 4: 4310ms and 4430ms drawn; 610ms and 730ms after a film) with the 1200ms unblur; invitation card names at 0.55s + i x 0.09s after data-in (i 4, 6) with the 1100ms rise.

motion.name: open-dissolve
motion.purpose: The drawn paper dissolves to opacity 0 over the scene.

motion.name: open-welcome
motion.purpose: Welcome lines and divider (i 0-2: 4300, 4440, 4580ms drawn) unblur from 6px at hero position.

motion.name: to-scene
motion.value: 5100ms (450ms under reduced motion; film: 1000ms after its last frame)
motion.purpose: TO_SCENE: the scene has the screen, sections mount, scroll unlocks, music coin fades in (800ms); shared between the component and the stylesheet. DRAWN_T0 3700ms sets --t0 for the drawn envelope.

motion.name: film-move-in
motion.purpose: Opening film, end 'card' (still available): the video translates and scales about opening.json's card rect until it covers the screen, then fades; with no first-screen card it now fades onto the photograph scene.

motion.name: film-tap
motion.purpose: The tap starts music, the film's sounds (playFilmSounds) and the muted inline film; the names and hint set over the poster fade out.

motion.name: film-sounds
motion.value: touch 50ms; tension knot - 0.7s/800ms/4.6kHz; knot/300ms/3.6kHz; ribbon/800ms/2.6kHz; doors/900ms/1.1kHz, 950Hz; flaps/800ms/1.5kHz; bells from end + i x 110ms
motion.purpose: playFilmSounds (src/lib/media.ts): the drawn opening's sounds placed on opening.json cues (seconds): knot 2.6, ribbon 2.95, doors 3.8 and 4.85, flaps 6.1, end 7.3.

motion.name: film-dissolve
motion.purpose: Opening film, end 'scene' (the current film): onHandover sets data-play with --t0 0ms, the film fades into the photograph scene, and is removed at 1000ms.

motion.name: film-watchdogs
motion.purpose: No visible start (currentTime > 0.05s) 2.5s after the tap: the drawn envelope takes over from its first beat. Stopped for 3s part-way: hands over where it is.

motion.name: coin-scrolling
motion.value: opacity and scale 0.35s; data-scrolling cleared 650ms after the last scroll
motion.purpose: While the page scrolls the music coin steps back (opacity 0.4, scale 0.86) from the content beneath it.

motion.name: scroll-cue
motion.purpose: At the foot of the hero photograph; chevron bobs 5px.

motion.name: ribbon-sounds
motion.value: noise 50ms/180ms/5.2kHz; 300ms/700ms/4.6kHz; 920ms/300ms/3.6kHz; 1150ms/900ms/2.6kHz; 2450ms and 2850ms/900ms/1.1kHz, 950Hz; 3700ms/700ms/1.5kHz; bells from 4400ms + i x 110ms
motion.purpose: playRibbonSounds: the touch, the tail drawn under tension, the knot giving, the flutter down, the two doors, the inner flaps, then four bells 2349, 2794, 3136, 3729Hz. The bells ring from 4400ms, as the paper gives way to the scene.

motion.name: ambient-petals
motion.purpose: Canvas of 11 petals falling and 16 amber motes rising (lighter); DPR capped at 2; pauses off screen and in a hidden tab; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: photo-drift
motion.purpose: Photograph drifts to translate(-1.6%, -1%).

motion.name: scratch-reveal
motion.value: 0.7s ease-out; pop 700ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.6, 0.5, 1); glint 1100ms ease-out after 150ms
motion.purpose: Foil fades once half is scratched; value pops from 0.82, a glint crosses the card, navigator.vibrate(12). All three scratched: gold-mote shower from the row centre for 1600ms.

motion.name: after-date
motion.purpose: Collapsed block opens after all three dates are revealed.

motion.name: spray-sway
motion.value: hero 5.5s ease-in-out infinite alternate (right -2.7s); message 6s after 1.4s
motion.purpose: Rose sprays rock ±1.6deg from their foot.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: [data-reveal] gains data-in on first entry; --d staggers. up: 22px + blur(4px), 1s ease-out.

motion.name: reveal-deal
motion.purpose: Date cards dealt from 38px low at -7deg, 2deg, 8deg.

motion.name: reveal-card
motion.value: 1.4s; lines 0.55s + --i x 0.09s (i 0-12), 1100ms ease-out each; sheen 9s after 2.4s
motion.purpose: Invitation card (.mh-card--section) laid down as it scrolls in from perspective(1100px) rotateX(16deg) translateY(50px) scale(0.96), pivoting on its foot; its lines rise in by --i and its names are written in. The gift card is laid down the same way; its sheen crosses every 7s after 1.1s.

motion.name: reveal-bloom
motion.purpose: Message sprays open from 0.7 scale, then sway.

motion.name: reveal-line-step
motion.value: line 2.6s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); art 1s, node pop 0.7s at 0.1s, text at 0.25s
motion.purpose: Programme hairline drawn down; art slides 28px from its side, the rings photograph wipes in with clip-path over 1.3s; text from the opposite side.

motion.name: pin-drop
motion.purpose: Venue pin drops 70px onto the map.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: Closing seal pressed from 1.9 scale and blur(3px) through 0.94 and 1.03; closing line and names written in at 700ms and 1200ms.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: card fades to the scene in 400ms; no film; everything else at rest
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. No film, hold, bow swell, hint breathing, untying, doors, flaps or camera; the photograph, its lettering and roses at rest; no petals, drift, sway or cue bob; every scroll reveal (the invitation card's lines and names included) marked in at once and shown without clip, mask, transform or transition.

components.name: Closing Wax Seal

components.name: Invitation Card
components.description: The card that was inside the envelope, laid on the page after the date (in the build .mh-card--section: the column less 20px, at most 420px, 3:5, 4px corners, the card-on-paper shadow): the envelope's embossed paper (paper.jpg via --mh-art) under a radial cream veil, a gold double rule, and the scene's rose spray (spray.jpg) multiplied into the top-left and bottom-right corners; here soft radials stand in for the rasters. Sepia script names, Bodoni italic verse and address, the template's divider, a date block; every size max(px floor, cqi), and the card grows taller on narrow phones.

narrative.overview:
The phone screen is the closed card, edge to edge: a gatefold of the owner's ivory paper blind-embossed with roses and climbing vines, its two doors meeting at a centre seam, the inner envelope's fold lines showing faintly through toward a point at 56% height. The couple's names are printed across both doors in bronze script at 35% height, a champagne satin ribbon crosses the card at 56% and is tied at the centre in a bow, and "Lentani torting" is set in small spaced capitals near the foot. Closed, the card is alive in the guest's hands: it tilts slowly and the bow swells and rocks as if inviting a touch. A fingertip presses softly into the paper where it lands; the guest can tap, or take the ribbon and pull, and the bow and band follow the finger under rubber-band tension and spring back if let go early. Untying it is the one orchestrated moment of the page, told in order: the pulled tail is drawn out and its loop slips through, the knot gives and the other loop follows, the bow rocks free and the satin flutters down, lands and crumples away; the left door is lifted at its edge, swung open with a slight flex and settles, then the right; the inner envelope's four flaps lift and fold back off the photograph, which comes into focus as the camera moves through; the names and the welcome are written in where they will sit in the hero, and the paper dissolves into a sunset photograph of the couple walking toward a mosque, where petals keep falling and light keeps rising. In the showcase the same story is told by the owner's own film: its first frame is the closed card (its satin is silver, the film's own), the couple's names and the hint are set over it in type, and on the tap it plays the bow untying and the doors and flaps opening, then dissolves into the same photograph.

After the opening the page is ceremonial, and each section arrives once as it scrolls in: one centred phone-width column on cream (#f5ecdf), sepia ink, gold script titles, rose sprays multiplied onto the ground so their white backgrounds vanish, and, after the date, an invitation card cut from the envelope's own embossed paper (quietened under a cream veil where the type sits, framed by a gold double rule, the scene's roses multiplied into two corners) that sets the Bismillah, the Rum 30:21 verse, the families, the names in sepia script, the date and the venue. The world is built from the owner's own rasters (photograph, paper, seal, roses, rings), each carrying its generation prompt and post-processing in embedded metadata; the owner's opening film is the one moving raster; code draws what the rasters do not cover (the satin ribbon and bow, the card's fold lines, the invitation card's rules and type, gold timeline line art, dividers, the venue map, icons).
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed embossed gatefold card tied with a satin bow as the first viewport (in the showcase, the owner's film poster with its silver satin; the drawn fallback in champagne satin); the whole card is the control, and it carries only the names and one hint line.
An owner-supplied raster world, each image carrying embedded provenance; nothing generic or stock. The invitation card reuses the same rasters (paper and rose spray) rather than bringing its own.
Gold is a material (foil, gilt edge, coin, pressed leaf, satin), rendered as gradients from deep antique to pale champagne, never as a flat accent fill and never on text.
Sepia ink throughout; no black anywhere a guest can see.
Three faces with fixed jobs: Corinthia script for names, greetings and section titles; Bodoni Moda for everything set; Amiri for the Arabic Bismillah alone.
The opening ends in the evening light: the paper, or the film, dissolves into the couple's photograph, which is the first screen; the invitation card is laid on the page after the date.

Slow exponential ease-out; a tied card that breathes in the hand, one choreographed untying and opening, sections that arrive once as the guest scrolls them in, two tactile interactions (pulling the ribbon, scratching the gold-foil date), otherwise only ambient motion (petals, rising light, drifting photograph, swaying roses). Reduced motion shows everything at rest.

rules.name: The Sepia Rule
rules.body: Ink is brown, never black. Even the showcase phone bezel is dark brown (#241a10). Nothing code draws is cool: the drawn satin ribbon is champagne, and its shadows are brown; the cool notes are in the owner's rasters (the photograph, and the opening film's silver satin).

rules.name: The Light Is Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Amber and the white-gold radials describe light (the focus halo on the bow, the rising motes and the date shower, the glints that cross the foil, the invitation card and the gift card, the sky veil behind the hero names, the cream glow behind the closed card's hint). They never fill a card, a button or text.

rules.name: The Multiply Rule
rules.body: Rasters drawn on white (rose spray, rings) are laid on cream with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` so their ground disappears, on the page and on the invitation card's paper alike; the seal's initials are gold (#a77b34, dot #b88c3e) multiplied into the wax so they read as pressed, not printed.

rules.name: The Spoken Script Rule
rules.body: Corinthia sets names, greetings, section titles and the programme times. Instructions, body copy, labels, form text and data are Bodoni Moda.

rules.name: The Bismillah Only Rule
rules.body: Amiri sets the Arabic Bismillah and nothing else, and it is fetched only for those glyphs.

rules.name: The Shares of the Card Rule
rules.body: Everything on the invitation card (type, rules, sprigs, gaps, the double rule's inset) is a share of the card's width in `cqi`, so the card scales whole like a printed one; each type size has a legible px floor (`max(px, cqi)`, nothing under 8.5px), and on the narrowest phones the card grows taller (its 3:5 ratio yields to content under `overflow: clip`) rather than letting the type shrink. Nothing inside it is sized in vw.

rules.name: The Printed Face Rule
rules.body: The closed card carries exactly two lines of text, both printed across the doors so they split at the seam: the couple's names in script and the hint line in spaced capitals. Over the opening film's poster the same two lines are set in type (names in bronze script at the film's `names` height, 0.2 for the current film; "Ochish uchun bosing" at its `hint` height, 0.86, default 0.8, in 12px Bodoni 500 spaced capitals at 0.32em, #6a5236 on a cream glow), so one film serves every couple. Everything else on the paper is the owner's embossing and the fold lines.

rules.name: The Real Paper Rule
rules.body: The closed card's relief is the owner's embossed-paper photograph, printed across both doors as one sheet (each door shows its half of a 200%-wide print, so the image runs unbroken across the seam). The inner envelope's flap faces are cut from the same print, multiplied over their paper gradients at 0.45 so their relief is fainter. Code adds only the fold lines, the seam, the printed names and the hint line; no coded relief, flourish or colour ornament. The ribbon lies on the paper; it is not printed on it.

rules.name: The Wipe, Not Fade Rule
rules.body: A multiplied photograph (rose spray, rings) never fades and never sits inside an ancestor that fades or transforms: Chrome drops the blend mid-fade and an ancestor's opacity isolates it, so the white ground flashes. Move the image itself, not its box, and draw it in with a clip-path wipe (`inset(0 100% 0 0)` to none, 1.3s ease-out, mirrored for right-hand art). Its own rotate or scale (the sway) is fine. The invitation card is the one allowed case: its sprays multiply onto the card's own paper, inside the card's group, so the card may be laid down with opacity and transform and the sprays ride with it. The sprays are part of the card's stock, present from the first frame the card is seen; they take no wipe of their own.

dos: Do keep every raster owner-supplied and carrying its prompt and post-processing in embedded metadata.
Do lay white-ground rasters on cream with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, and press the seal's initials into the wax the same way.
Do render gold as a gradient material with a highlight and a darker edge (deep antique to pale champagne), not as a flat fill.
Do time motion with the slow ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`), and tell the opening in order: the bow undone, the ribbon gone, the doors, the inner flaps, then the scene.
Do let the satin answer the finger: tension that gives and then resists, a spring back with a slight overshoot when let go early, and an untying that starts from the pulled side.
Do draw icons, sparks, dividers and nodes as inline SVG in line gold or currentColor.
Do keep fixed controls aligned to the 480px column and clear of safe-area insets.
Do size everything inside the invitation card in `cqi` of the card with a legible px floor (`max(px, cqi)`), and let the card grow taller rather than shrink its type.

Do honour reduced motion: the closed card is still (no hold, bow swell or breathing hint), a tap fades it to the scene in 400ms, there is no film, the photograph's lettering, photograph and roses stand at rest, and there are no petals, drift, sway or cue bob; every scroll reveal is shown at rest.
Do bring each section in once, as the guest scrolls to it, and leave it in place.
Do draw a multiplied photograph in with a clip-path wipe on the image itself.
donts: Don't print colour ornament or extra text on the closed card; it carries the embossed paper, its fold lines, the printed names, one hint line and the satin bow.

Don't use black ink, or grey or cool tones in anything code draws; text is sepia, and even the drawn satin ribbon is champagne (the silver satin in the owner's film is the film's own material, not a licence for coded silver).
Don't fill text with a gradient or clip a gradient to text; gold text is a flat script gold or bronze.
Don't use emoji or font glyphs as icons.
Don't let the hand-over jump: the opening (the paper, or the film) dissolves into the live scene already composed beneath it, which is coming into focus as the dissolve begins.
Don't add a second automatic sequence after the opening; later motion answers the guest (a section scrolled into view, a date scratched) or is ambient.
Don't fade a multiplied photograph or fade or transform any ancestor of one whose backdrop lies outside it; Chrome drops the blend and its white ground shows.
Don't set instructions, body copy, labels or form text in the script face, or use Amiri for anything but the Bismillah.
Don't let a later template borrow these tokens, rasters, the opening film, the satin bow, the seal, the invitation card or the gift card; it shares only the showcase shell.
